descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · S20 A phone call, backgrounding or a screen lock mid-dictation loses no text

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T4 Native microphone dictation works on iOS and Android and survives a phone call, backgrounding or a screen lock with no text lost. (TFA-92570 AC 3; TFA-92570 AC 5)
  • T6 No dictated fact is silently dropped (Principle 2), including the last words before Stop and the words around an interruption or a recovery. (TFA-94229 R9) — gate: blocked: TFA-94229 in progress
  • T3 Dictation does not crash the tab. (TFA-94423 AC 8)
  • U1 Dictated numbers (doses, lab values, vital signs) are transcribed exactly: same value, nothing dropped, added or changed. (UAT TC-23; TFA-94423 AC 3)
  • U4 U1-U3 hold on both Wi-Fi and cellular. (UAT TC-23; TFA-94423 AC 6)
  • T1 GPT-live is the active dictation engine on every platform (no on-device or native recogniser on phones either, Daniela 2026-10-09), routed server-side, with no API key in the browser. (TFA-94423 AC 1; TFA-94423 latest decision (Daniela 2026-10-09))

Test design technique: Device (device) — Look at the layout and gestures at phone size or on a real device (iPhone / Pixel).

Given Same devices and build as S19

When Dictate H-03 and mid-sentence (a) take a phone call, (b) send the app to the background, (c) lock the screen, (d) start on Wi-Fi and turn Wi-Fi off mid-sentence so the phone moves to cellular; return to the app each time

Then Every word spoken before the interruption (for (d): every word) reaches the box exactly once, or the Recover control is offered and recovers it exactly once; the app does not crash; Dictate works again afterwards; the engine of each take and of any recovered text is recorded

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): TFA-92570 AC 5 (no text lost), TFA-94423 AC 8 (no crash), TFA-94229 R9; the recovered text keeps its S01 checks; engine of the recovered text recorded (Q6); a take with no gpt-live-transcribe row is a Fail of T1. (d) covers U4 for a network change during a take; a throttled browser is no substitute (Q5)

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S20 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-23.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16/17 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on dev; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-23/S20

A phone call, backgrounding or a screen lock mid-dictation loses no text

Tickets: TFA-92570 Mobile: Capacitor wrap for App Store & Google Play (ready for qa); TFA-94229 Port & preserve Vikram's clinical AI logic (in progress); TFA-94423 Implement GPT-live medical mode for active dictation (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status blocked in newspec-c/results.json → blocked (blocked).

Detail:

Not runnable on the emulator: it needs words actually dictated (and transcribed by gpt-live) when the call / background / lock / Wi-Fi-to-cellular switch happens, the Recover control, and the engine of each take; the emulator has no microphone input, no cellular, and the live transcription session must not be opened on the local stack. What the emulator did show (OAT-03/S20 run, typed stand-in): typed text survives a 30 s lock, 30 s in the background and an incoming call in both contexts, and the app does not crash.

Evidence: 15 attached.

Dev run: skipped: set-aside — set-aside: iOS/Android; dictation by microphone/speaker (Quinn 2026-10-14) — A phone call, backgrounding, a screen lock and a Wi-Fi-to-cellular switch on real iPhone / Android phones while dictating by microphone: microphone/speaker, iOS and Android are set aside for the dev run (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
